# HAProxy — custom-to-root-context-push-url

custom-to-root-context with VAADIN_PUSH_URL=/VAADIN/push. The browser asks for /app/VAADIN/push and the same prefix strip that carries every other request hands /VAADIN/push to the backend.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/app/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

HAProxy config (`haproxy/templates/strip-prefix.cfg`), mounted as
`conf.d/10-vaadin.cfg`:

```haproxy
# Proxy at /app/, app at the backend root: the public URL carries a prefix the
# backend knows nothing about. Shared by custom-to-root-context and
# custom-to-root-context-push-url, which differ only in VAADIN_PUSH_URL.
#
# Both halves of the translation are here. On the way in the prefix is stripped;
# on the way out the two things the backend says about its own location — the
# Location header and every cookie's Path — are put back by raw regex, because
# HAProxy has no ProxyPassReverse, no ProxyPassReverseCookiePath, no
# proxy_redirect and no proxy_cookie_path. Compare traefik/http/
# custom-to-root-context, which cannot rewrite a response at all and documents
# the resulting broken redirect instead.
frontend vaadin-in from vaadin-front
    bind :80

    # A frontend sees every path, so the published prefix has to be enforced
    # rather than declared: the NGINX sibling has a `location /app/` and nothing
    # else, and without this deny the backend would answer at / as well.
    acl is_app path /app
    acl is_app path_beg /app/
    http-request deny deny_status 404 unless is_app

    # /app -> /, /app/foo -> /foo. The optional slash keeps the bare prefix
    # working without a redirect to add a trailing one.
    http-request replace-path ^/app/?(.*) /\1

    default_backend vaadin-app

backend vaadin-app from vaadin
    http-response replace-header Location ^(https?://[^/]+)?/(.*) \1/app/\2
    # Anchored on the end of the value rather than on what follows the path:
    # Tomcat writes `Path=/; HttpOnly`, so a regex expecting another path
    # segment after the slash matches nothing at all — and a rewrite that
    # matches nothing looks exactly like a rewrite that was not needed, right
    # up until the browser stops sending the session cookie back.
    #
    # Note the literal space in a character class would break the config
    # parser before the regex engine ever saw it; \s is the way to write it.
    http-response replace-header Set-Cookie (.*;\s*[Pp]ath=)/(;.*)?$ \1/app\2
    server vaadin vaadin:8080
```

The `global` section, and the two `defaults` sections this file
inherits from, come from the shared
[haproxy-base.cfg](../../haproxy-base.cfg), mounted read-only beside
it as `conf.d/00-base.cfg`. Base and scenario only parse as a pair.
